quests.prompt: Write one sentence about sending a message and getting a reply.
quests.sampleAnswer: I sent a text to my friend, and she replied a few hours later.
quests.hint: Think about a message you sent and what happened afterward.
quests.explanation: The connector 'and' joins two related actions into one clear, simple sentence.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about calling someone who could not answer.
quests.sampleAnswer: I tried to call my sister, but she was busy, so I left a voicemail.
quests.hint: Think about a call that didn't go through and what you did next.
quests.explanation: The connectors 'but' and 'so' link three related ideas smoothly into one natural sentence.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about inviting a friend to an event.
quests.sampleAnswer: I sent an invite for my party, and my friend was really excited.
quests.hint: Think about how a friend reacted to being invited somewhere.
quests.explanation: Pairing an action with a reaction using 'and' makes a simple sentence feel complete and natural.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about doing chores at home.
quests.sampleAnswer: I did the laundry and washed the dishes, so now I feel quite tired.
quests.hint: Think about two chores you did and how you feel afterward.
quests.explanation: Joining two actions with 'and' before adding a result with 'so' is a simple way to build a longer sentence.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about your weekend plans changing.
quests.sampleAnswer: I had a plan to go out, but it started to rain, so I stayed home.
quests.hint: Think about an outdoor plan that was changed by the weather.
quests.explanation: This sentence uses 'but' and 'so' together to show a clear cause-and-effect chain in everyday language.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about cleaning your room.
quests.sampleAnswer: My room was messy this morning, but now it looks neat because I cleaned it.
quests.hint: Think about how a space looked before and after you cleaned it.
quests.explanation: Contrasting 'before' and 'after' with 'but' is a simple, effective way to show change in a sentence.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about how you felt during a test.
quests.sampleAnswer: I felt nervous before the exam, but I was relieved when it was over.
quests.hint: Think about your feelings before and after a stressful test.
quests.explanation: Using two feeling adjectives connected by 'but' shows how an emotion can change over time.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about how a class made you feel.
quests.sampleAnswer: I was bored during the long lecture, but the science class made me excited.
quests.hint: Think about one class you find boring and one you find exciting.
quests.explanation: Comparing two different feelings about two classes makes the sentence more specific and interesting.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about presenting in front of your class.
quests.sampleAnswer: I am usually shy, but I felt proud after finishing my presentation.
quests.hint: Think about a personality trait and how an achievement changed your feeling.
quests.explanation: This sentence shows personal growth in a single sentence by contrasting a usual trait with a specific moment.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about how a busy day at work felt.
quests.sampleAnswer: I felt stressed during the busy morning, but I finally relaxed in the afternoon.
quests.hint: Think about how your mood changed during one work day.
quests.explanation: Showing an emotional shift from morning to afternoon makes a simple work journal entry feel realistic.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about receiving good news at work.
quests.sampleAnswer: I was surprised and very happy when I heard about my promotion.
quests.hint: Think about good news you received and how it made you feel.
quests.explanation: Listing two positive feelings together strengthens the emotional impact of good news in writing.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about a difficult task at work.
quests.sampleAnswer: I felt confused about the new task at first, but now I feel confident.
quests.hint: Think about a task that was hard to understand but later made sense.
quests.explanation: Contrasting confusion with confidence shows progress, which makes the writing more engaging.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about a trip you are planning.
quests.sampleAnswer: I am going to the beach with my family this weekend.
quests.hint: Think about a short trip you have already decided to take soon.
quests.explanation: 'Going to' is the simplest way to talk about a plan that is already decided.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about a place you plan to visit next year.
quests.sampleAnswer: Next year, I am going to visit a new country for the first time.
quests.hint: Think about a travel goal you have for the near future.
quests.explanation: Adding a time phrase like 'next year' makes a future plan feel more specific and real.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about preparing for an upcoming trip.
quests.sampleAnswer: I am going to pack my suitcase tomorrow morning before the trip.
quests.hint: Think about a task you plan to do right before you travel.
quests.explanation: This sentence uses 'going to' with a clear time word, 'tomorrow,' to show a near-future plan.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about a family event you are planning.
quests.sampleAnswer: We are going to visit my grandparents this Sunday afternoon.
quests.hint: Think about a family visit you already have planned.
quests.explanation: 'Going to' clearly expresses a decided plan involving family members.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about a celebration your family is planning.
quests.sampleAnswer: My family is going to celebrate my sister's birthday next week.
quests.hint: Think about an upcoming celebration in your family.
quests.explanation: Using 'going to' with a specific event makes the future plan clear and easy to picture.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence about a family meal you are planning.
quests.sampleAnswer: This weekend, my family is going to cook dinner together.
quests.hint: Think about a meal your family plans to make as a group.
quests.explanation: Adding 'together' shows that the planned activity involves more than one person, which adds detail.

quests.prompt: Answer this question in one sentence: What did you buy recently?
quests.sampleAnswer: I bought a warm jacket from a store near my house.
quests.hint: Think about a recent purchase and where you got it.
quests.explanation: Answering a Wh- question directly with a simple past sentence is good practice for clear, complete writing.

quests.prompt: Answer this question in one sentence: Why did you return an item?
quests.sampleAnswer: I returned the shoes because the size was wrong.
quests.hint: Think about a reason you once had to return something you bought.
quests.explanation: Using 'because' to answer a 'why' question directly is a simple, clear way to explain a reason.

quests.prompt: Answer this question in one sentence: What do you usually buy at the supermarket?
quests.sampleAnswer: I usually buy fresh groceries and a few snacks at the supermarket.
quests.hint: Think about the items that are always on your shopping list.
quests.explanation: The word 'usually' signals a habit, which directly answers a question about routine behavior.

quests.prompt: Answer this question in one sentence: What did you cook last night?
quests.sampleAnswer: Last night, I cooked rice with grilled chicken for dinner.
quests.hint: Think about the last meal you actually prepared yourself.
quests.explanation: Answering with a time word and a simple past verb makes a clear, direct response to the question.

quests.prompt: Answer this question in one sentence: Why do you like a certain restaurant?
quests.sampleAnswer: I like that restaurant because the staff is friendly and the food is delicious.
quests.hint: Think of two reasons you enjoy going to a particular restaurant.
quests.explanation: Giving two reasons after 'because' makes an opinion sound more convincing and complete.

quests.prompt: Answer this question in one sentence: What is something you have never tried?
quests.sampleAnswer: I have never tried sushi, but I want to soon.
quests.hint: Think of a food you haven't eaten yet but are curious about.
quests.explanation: The present perfect 'have never tried' is the natural way to talk about a lifetime experience.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence giving your opinion about social media.
quests.sampleAnswer: I think social media can be addictive because it's so easy to keep scrolling.
quests.hint: Think about why social media can be hard to put down.
quests.explanation: The pattern 'I think...because' is a simple but powerful way to state and support an opinion.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence giving your opinion about online shopping.
quests.sampleAnswer: I think online shopping is convenient because I can buy things from home.
quests.hint: Think about why shopping online saves you time or effort.
quests.explanation: Supporting an opinion with a clear reason after 'because' makes a simple sentence more persuasive.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence giving your opinion about smartphones in class.
quests.sampleAnswer: I think phones in class are distracting because students check messages constantly.
quests.hint: Think about why phones might make it hard to focus during lessons.
quests.explanation: This sentence models how to state a simple opinion and justify it with one clear reason.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence giving your opinion about sleep.
quests.sampleAnswer: I think sleep is really important because it helps me focus the next day.
quests.hint: Think about why getting enough rest matters to you personally.
quests.explanation: The 'I think...because' structure helps beginners express and support an opinion clearly.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence giving your opinion about drinking water.
quests.sampleAnswer: I think drinking enough water is healthy because it keeps my body energized.
quests.hint: Think about one benefit you notice when you drink enough water.
quests.explanation: Stating a benefit after 'because' turns a simple opinion into a more convincing statement.

quests.prompt: Write one sentence giving your opinion about regular exercise.
quests.sampleAnswer: I think regular exercise gives me more energy because it wakes up my whole body.
quests.hint: Think about how moving your body changes the way you feel.
quests.explanation: This sentence shows how a simple cause-and-effect reason can strengthen a basic personal opinion.
